scope: Where the Rust rewrite's structure still differs from the Go owner it ports. Known source-confirmed gaps only, not an exhaustive acceptance claim.

findings.group: Structure: Go's shape before more ports
findings.finding: `pkg/sessiontxn` is ported as `tidb-sessiontxn` (2026-11-19): `TxnManager` holds one provider per transaction (`Optimistic`, `PessimisticRR`, `PessimisticRC`, `PessimisticSerializable`, `StalenessTxnContextProvider`, chosen as `newProviderWithRequest`), which owns the transaction and answers each statement's snapshot, `OnStmtStart` (RCCheckTS), `OnStmtRetry` (the for-update timestamp) and `OnStmtErrorForNextAction` (pessimistic lock errors, the after-query retry). Remaining: (1) the statement lifecycle opens the statement's snapshot before it compiles (`with_bound_statement` -> `open_read_snapshot` -> `run`), where Go compiles, advises (`AdviseOptimizeWithPlan`), builds (activating the transaction) and then reads; so the optimistic provider's max-ts point get is decided from the AST (`classify.rs` `statement_read_shape_bound` -> `AutocommitPointGet`, `open_read_snapshot`'s arm) instead of from the plan (`IsPointGetWithPKOrUniqueKeyByAutoCommit`); (2) Go enters every transaction through `TxnManager.EnterNewTxn(request)` -> `newProviderWithRequest` -> `OnInitialize`, while `TxnManager` has one entry per case (`open`, `enter_pending`, `enter_implicit_write` / `_read`, `enter_stale`) that builds the transaction before the provider wraps it (`decide_txn_mode` itself runs where Go's `PrepareTxnCtx` runs it).

findings.group: Structure: Go's shape before more ports
findings.finding: `mysql.*` tables have two access paths. Go reads and writes every system table through SQL on an internal session (`ExecRestrictedSQL` / `sess.Execute`): the DDL job queue, DDL history, reorg handles, delete ranges, the MDL info, the privilege load (`cache.go` `LoadAll`), `mysql.global_variables`, the statistics tables and the bootstrap rows. This port also has a direct key/value reader and writer, `tidb-syssession`'s `SystemTableView` (`mysql_system_tables.rs`) and `system_row_write.rs`, which decode and encode rows through `TableCommon` with their own default materialization, casting and handle-layout choice (`HandleLayout::of`). The DDL's production steps already run Go's SQL (every job step has a session) and the MDL check reads `mysql.tidb_mdl_info` through SQL; the DDL tables' row encoders (`plan_insert_attempt`, `finish_ddl_job`, the `get_ddl_reorg_handle` fallback, `DdlHistoryTable`) are still reached by the session-less planning mode `tidb-ddl/tests`, `tidb-session/tests` and the bootstrap planner's tests use. Production callers still on the direct path: `tidb-privilege` `cluster_privilege_load.rs`, `tidb-syssession` `cluster_sysvar_load.rs` (writes go through SQL), `tidb-stats-handle-storage` `cluster_stats_write.rs`, `tidb-executor` `cluster_analyze.rs`, `tidb-session` `mysql_bootstrap/rows.rs`, and the bindings. Whatever the SQL layer does on Go's path (request source and resource group, assertions, constraint checks, statement memory, `tidb_txn_assertion_level`) has to be repeated or is missing on the direct one.
findings.rust_evidence: `rust/crates/tidb-syssession/src/mysql_system_tables.rs`, `system_row_write.rs`, and the callers named in the gap

findings.group: Structure: Go's shape before more ports
findings.finding: The test tier still runs beside the store-backed one. `tidb-kv`'s `MemTableStorage` (no transaction, `do_lock_keys` a no-op), `tidb-table`'s `LocalTableAutoIds` / `tidb-autoid` `LocalAutoIdStore`, `LocalSequenceCounter`, `tidb-session`'s `SharedCatalog` and `tidb-executor`'s `run_create_table_on` (a CREATE TABLE without a DDL job, compiled only under `test` / `test-util`) give the executor's tests a second storage, allocator and DDL implementation; Go has one path, `mockstore` through the same `kv.Transaction`, meta allocators and DDL jobs as production. Progress (2026-11-19): the Go-ported executor test files now run as Go's TestKit SQL in `tidb-session/tests` (one file per Go file, Go test names: join, hash join, executor issues, insert, batch point-get, `executor_test.go`, partition table, parallel apply, plan cache, seqtest prepared, `prepared_test.go`, aggregate, merge join, memtest, oomtest (over Go's `oomCapture` log core), `pkg/table` partition), and their executor copies are gone. Remaining (42 files, ~365 tests still build over `run_create_table_on` / `MemTableStorage`): `tidb-executor/src/driver/tests/*` and `tidb-executor/tests/*` (Rust-only; the SQL-visible ones move to TestKit, tier-internal ones go), `kv_table/tests*.rs`, `tests_table_part1/2` (Go `pkg/table/tables` tests that drive `AddRecord`/`IterRecords` on the session transaction -- the TestKit needs Go's `sessiontxn.NewTxn` / `Session().Txn(true)` surface), `tests_executor_part22` (`TestInsertIgnore` needs `kv.NewInjectedStore` over the session store), `tests_merge_join_in_disk` (`join_pkg_test.go`'s mock-data-source tests belong in the executor's unit tests over mock sources); then the tier itself goes.

findings.group: Structure: Go's shape before more ports
findings.finding: A variable's Set behavior now lives on the variable for its warnings and session fields: `SysVarDef` carries Go's `Validation` (with a `VarsContext` for sibling reads and statement warnings), `set_session` and `set_global` hooks; `set_hooks.rs`'s deprecation-warning switch, the prune-mode / MPP-compression / hashagg-spill hooks, `tidb_enforce_mpp` and plan-replayer checks, and `SessionVars::set_session_from_hook`'s thirty typed-field branches moved onto their variables (2026-11-19). Also on their variables now (2026-11-19 late): `checkIsolationLevel`, `checkReadOnly` (the noop-gated ON switches), `max_allowed_packet`'s SET-only read-only refusal and `require_secure_transport`'s TLS / SEM refusal, through a `VarsContext` that carries Go's `vars` (the session's values in every scope, the statement type, the TLS state). Each variable has one `SetGlobal`, run on the validated value before the store for GLOBAL and INSTANCE writes as Go's `SetGlobalFromHook` is: its own (`tidb_schema_cache_size`, `tidb_redact_log`) or the one the node registers for it (the GC, MV-service and MDL switches, Go's `RegisterSysVar` from another package). Go's `GetSession` is on `SysVarDef` too (2026-11-19 night): the session-state reads (`timestamp`, `warning_count`, `error_count`, `last_insert_id` / `identity`, `tidb_current_ts` over `TxnCtx.StartTS` now on `SessionVars`, `tidb_last_txn_info` / `_query_info` / `_ddl_info`, `last_plan_from_cache` / `_binding`, `last_sql_use_alloc`, `rand_seed1` / `2`, `tidb_last_plan_replayer_token`) answer every session read -- `@@x`, `SHOW VARIABLES`, the variable tables -- where three name switches answered some surfaces (`SHOW VARIABLES` reported `warning_count` 0 and `timestamp` 0). `GetGlobal` is on `SysVarDef` as well, `global_get_hook` dispatching on it (the LDAP variables read their impls; the bind passwords read back masked, while `mysql.global_variables` keeps the value). Thirty-one `vardef`-backed variables (the TTL knobs, the DDL reorg and flashback knobs, the foreign-key / checksum / check-constraint / fast-reorg / auto-analyze / instance-plan-cache / fast-create-table switches, connection and memory limits, ...) carry Go's `SetGlobal` and `GetGlobal` over their process state, and the domain's `apply_set_global_hook` runs each variable's own `SetGlobal` first (2026-11-19 late night). So do 13 more (the OOM action, the alarm ratio, the force priority, the TiKV client's commit batch size and store limit, `require_secure_transport`, `tidb_check_mb4_value_in_utf8`, the service scope, resource control, the TTL window bounds, the reserved percentage and the PD circuit-breaker ratio, with Go's formatting and range refusals). So do the analyze default buckets / TopN, the auto-analyze priority queue, `tidb_enable_ts_validation`, the committer concurrency, `tidb_schema_cache_size` (with Go's origin text) and `tidb_redact_log`'s process-wide redaction (2026-11-19 night). The PD client options call Go's `variable.SetPDClientDynamicOption` / `SetLowResolutionTSOUpdateInterval` slots, which the domain fills (`initDomainSysVars`) and which store `vardef`'s values their `GetGlobal` read (2026-11-19 night). The statement-summary variables call `stmtsummaryv2`'s setters and the memory-arbitration variables set the process limit and arbitrator from their own `SetGlobal` (2026-11-19 night). The sysvar cache rebuild runs each variable's one `SetGlobal`, its own or the one registered for it (`SwitchMDL`, the MV service, the workload repository), as Go's `rebuildSysVarCache` does, so the domain's hook names no variable any more, and the live table's read answers each variable's own `GetGlobal` where the domain kept a `runtime_global_value` name switch (2026-11-20). Remaining: `runtime_instance_value` still names the INSTANCE-scope variables whose Go `GetGlobal` reads the instance config (the log, plugin, slow-log, expensive-query and statement-summary file settings); in all, about 74 of Go's 141 `GetGlobal` hooks have no counterpart -- Go keeps their value in a process atomic or the instance config (`vardef.PasswordValidationLength`, `ExpensiveQueryTimeThreshold`, `EnableNoopVariables`, the slow / general log and plugin settings, the GC variables in `mysql.tidb`, the memory limit and GOGC tuner, ...) which its readers consult, where this port keeps the global table as the one authority its readers read; Go's other `GetSession` hooks read typed fields this port keeps only in `systems`; (fixed 2026-11-19 late night: a session's load of the global session cache and the restore of a statement-scoped write run each variable's `SetSession` -- Go's `SetSystemVarWithRelaxedValidation` / `SetSystemVar` -- where 26 `*_from_systems` re-derivations and a charset/collation pairing function stood; the pairing is the six charset and collation variables' own `SetSession`); `autocommit`'s `SetSession` ending the transaction stays in `tidb-session` `variables.rs`, because Go's `SetInTxn` flag is transaction state this port keeps on the session (the `rand_seed` generator is `SessionVars.Rng` with its `SetSession` hooks, 2026-11-19 late night); (`tidb-exprstatic` loads its system variables into a real `SessionVars` through `SetSystemVar`, as Go's `newSessionVarsWithSystemVariables` does, since 2026-11-19 late night; `StaticSessionVars` is gone.)

Materialized views are ported up to their statements (phases in `rust/docs/go-shape-refactors-execplan.md`): `TableInfo` keeps Go master's `materialized_view*` fields byte for byte, the base table's DML writes its MV log rows as Go's does, the action types, schema diffs and `tidb_mview_*` / `tidb_mlog_*` variables are Go master's, and the parser takes every materialized view statement (CREATE / ALTER / DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW [LOG], REFRESH, PURGE, CANCEL, COMPARE, the SHOW forms) with Go master's restore text and syntax errors. `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW LOG`, `DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW LOG` and `ALTER MATERIALIZED VIEW LOG` (PURGE and ADD COLUMN) run as Go master's do, DROP / TRUNCATE / RENAME TABLE, ALTER TABLE, CREATE / DROP / ALTER INDEX, PARTITION BY, REMOVE PARTITIONING and EXCHANGE PARTITION refuse a log and its base table as Go master's do, MODIFY / CHANGE COLUMN of a logged base table retypes the log's tracked column as Go master's does (a base table with dependent materialized views is refused until those are ported), (the log table Go builds, the base table's `MaterializedViewBase`, the `mysql.tidb_mlog_purge_info` row with its schedule, Go's refusals and the `tidb_mview_enable` gate); on a base table that is itself a materialized view the DDL session holds the view's refresh advisory lock for the job's delivery, as Go master's does. CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW runs as Go master's does: the planner's SELECT build and column count, `validateCreateMaterializedViewQuery` (via `tidb-mviewutil`), the view table from the SELECT's output types with its group key and `MaterializedViewInfo`, the owner's create step and its initial build, the refresh and refresh-source rows, and the rollback of a failed build. ALTER MATERIALIZED VIEW (COMMENT, REFRESH with its schedule row, ATTRIBUTES) and DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW run as Go master's do too. The build runs Go's INSERT path (`REPLACE INTO view <definition>`); Go's TiKV store builds by IMPORT INTO instead, which this node does not run for it. `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW ... COMPLETE IN PLACE` runs as Go master's does (advisory lock, refresh-info row lock, history rows, DELETE + INSERT of the definition, refresh-source baseline, success persist, failure alert), and so does COMPLETE OUT OF PLACE (shadow table, build, cutover DDL, shadow cleanup), except the TiKV store's IMPORT INTO build (this port builds by INSERT); under the advisory lock a refresh reloads the node's schema when a committed DDL touches the view, its sources or their logs (`ensureMVRefreshSchemaVersion`, Go `TestMaterializedViewRefreshSchemaVersion`). Go master after this port's `eca4674a6f` baseline: nested materialized views (`27b1b52535f`: a ready view as a source, `validateMaterializedViewSourceState` / `validateMaterializedViewNestingDepth` / `validateMaterializedViewSourceMLog`, `ResolveFastRefreshSource`) are ported with Go's `mviewnested` create tests; still to port are `36b2c7f57ec` (OUT OF PLACE refresh of a view with a log or dependent views: the cutover, delete-range, notifier, GC and stats changes, so `TestMaterializedViewRefreshSchemaVersion`'s `source_oop` scenario does not run), `6aec16d0234` (DDL safeguards), `0a914c5b134` (maintenance error codes) and `357915c30e7` (MLog column additions serialized with refresh). COMPLETE DELTA APPLY (over FULL OUTER JOIN), PURGE MATERIALIZED VIEW LOG, CANCEL MATERIALIZED VIEW JOB with the task monitor, COMPARE MATERIALIZED VIEW and the SHOW forms run as Go master's do, and a user statement's writes to a view, its log or its shadow table are refused outside maintenance as Go master's are (`CheckMViewUpdatable` / `CheckMViewReadable`, ANALYZE's included). REFRESH ... DRY RUN and WITH PROFILE run as Go master's do. FAST refresh runs as Go master's does (the planner's merge source over the log window with Go's commit-ts window estimate, the delta merge executor with MIN / MAX recomputed through the full-update index lookup, AS OF targets, the log baseline and integrity checks, its DRY RUN and PROFILE), except an AS OF FAST refresh whose MIN / MAX must be recomputed, which this node refuses (Go reads the base table at the target snapshot there). `MAX_COUNT` / `MIN_COUNT` run as internal aggregates (Go master's `func_max_min_count.go`, window slide included), but this parser does not yet take them as SQL functions as Go master's does. This branch's bootstrap does not create Go master's five materialized view tables (`mysql.tidb_mview_refresh_info` .. `tidb_mlog_purge_hist`, Go master's `upgradeToVer316`). The mview background service (`pkg/mvservice`) runs as Go master's does (scheduled FAST refresh and log purge, MV log auto-analyze, history GC, refresh alerts, accumulation counts, its sysvars). IMPORT INTO depends on them in one place: a next-gen IMPORT INTO ... FROM SELECT runs on a DXF worker (`ImportStepQuery`) only during materialized-view maintenance (`InMViewMaintenance`), so this port refuses every next-gen FROM SELECT, as Go does outside maintenance, and `ImportStepQuery` is not ported.

findings.finding: The next-gen keyspace services are absent. `--standby`, `--activation-timeout`, `--max-idle-seconds` and `--keyspace-activate` are parsed into `cfg.standby` / `cfg.keyspace_activate_mode` and never read, so a standby node serves at once (Go `pkg/standby`'s `LoadKeyspaceController`: `WaitForActivate`, the activation HTTP API, the idle watcher, `exitAfterKeyspaceActivate`, via `pkg/tidbmanager`). The external workload manager (`pkg/extworkload`) exists only as seam traits (`tidb-gcworker` `GcV2Manager`, the TTL job manager's boundary) with no implementation and `main.go`'s `initExternalWorkloadManager` has no counterpart. `pkg/metaservice` (per-keyspace meta service group discovery used by the TiKV driver) has no counterpart. The DXF cleanup does not send `SendRowAndSizeMeterData` (`tidb-dxf-handle` header). The starter deployment's `/owner_manager/auto_id_service` route (Go `NewAutoIDOwnerHandler`: 500 unless `Server.Health()`, else `is_owner` of the AutoID service) and `Server.Close`'s standby-controller condition on `AutoIDServiceClose` are absent too: this port has no `Server.health` flag or standby controller (the AutoID service itself is served, N07 closed 2026-11-19).
